title: Product Price Range Histogram
description:
Bucket all products into four price ranges and count how many fall in each bucket: `'0-50'`, `'51-150'`, `'151-300'`, and `'301+'`.

**Table: products** — `product_id`, `product_name`, `price`

Output columns: `price_range`, `product_count`. Order by the minimum price in each bucket (ascending).
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (product_id INTEGER, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Budget Phone',49.99),(2,'Basic Tablet',79.99),(3,'Mid Phone',149.99),(4,'Standard Tablet',199.99),(5,'Premium Phone',349.99),(6,'Basic Laptop',499.99),(7,'Gaming Mouse',29.99),(8,'Mechanical Keyboard',89.99),(9,'Monitor 24in',249.99),(10,'Gaming Chair',399.99),(11,'Headphones',59.99),(12,'Webcam',39.99);
solution_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN price <= 50 THEN '0-50' WHEN price <= 150 THEN '51-150' WHEN price <= 300 THEN '151-300' ELSE '301+' END AS price_range, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY CASE WHEN price <= 50 THEN '0-50' WHEN price <= 150 THEN '51-150' WHEN price <= 300 THEN '151-300' ELSE '301+' END ORDER BY MIN(price);
hints: Use a CASE WHEN expression in both SELECT and GROUP BY to define the buckets.
ORDER BY MIN(price) ensures the buckets are ordered from cheapest to most expensive.
When grouping by a CASE expression, you must repeat the full CASE WHEN logic in the GROUP BY clause.
explanation: '0-50': Budget Phone (49.99), Gaming Mouse (29.99), Webcam (39.99) = 3 products. '51-150': Basic Tablet (79.99), Mid Phone (149.99), Headphones (59.99), Mechanical Keyboard (89.99) = 4 products. '151-300': Standard Tablet (199.99), Monitor (249.99) = 2 products. '301+': Premium Phone (349.99), Basic Laptop (499.99), Gaming Chair (399.99) = 3 products.
